clusters.rule: Directional transitional states must map to distinct icons in icons.json, matching how cover distinguishes opening from closing.
clusters.trigger: An icons.json state block that adds both `opening` and `closing` (or equivalent paired transitional states) pointing at the same mdi icon.

clusters.rule: Do not feature-detect attributes on the integration's own pinned library with hasattr/getattr/callable; the manifest requirement pins the version, so call the API directly.
clusters.trigger: A setup or platform filter such as `if callable(getattr(node, "method", None))` applied to objects from the integration's requirement package.

clusters.rule: Diagnostics output should expose internal library and connection data that is not otherwise reachable, not a dump of device and entity registry information.
clusters.trigger: async_get_config_entry_diagnostics building lists of device names with their entities from the device/entity registry.

clusters.rule: Set only the _attr_* entity attributes; do not additionally assign the legacy private counterparts such as _name alongside _attr_name.
clusters.trigger: An entity __init__ assigning both self._attr_name and self._name (or another duplicated legacy attribute) to the same value.

clusters.rule: Every translation_key an entity references must have a matching entry under `entity` in the integration's strings.json, added in the same PR and never removed while the key is still used.
clusters.trigger: A new or renamed entity description whose translation_key has no strings.json entry, or a strings.json diff deleting the `name` under a key that code still sets as translation_key.

clusters.rule: Entities whose state is bool | None need tests that separate missing data (unknown) from an explicit zero/false reading.
clusters.trigger: A new is_on/native_value property returning None for absent data and a boolean otherwise, with fixtures covering only the populated case.

clusters.rule: Normalize loosely typed device API values explicitly: compare feature flags and on/off states against the full set of representations the API uses (True, 1, "1") instead of relying on truthiness or a partial literal set.
clusters.trigger: Entity gating written as `if not all(coordinator.get_value(path) ...)` or a state check written as `value in (True, "1")` against a JSON API that also returns ints and numeric strings.

clusters.rule: Declare list-valued service schema fields with a real voluptuous list validator such as vol.All(cv.ensure_list, [str]), never with a bare Python type annotation like list[str].
clusters.trigger: A vol.Schema in an integration's services.py using a typing construct (list[str], dict[str, str]) as the validator for a Required/Optional key.

clusters.rule: Resolve a config entry from a service call with the core helper homeassistant.helpers.service.async_get_config_entry instead of hand-rolling entry-exists / correct-domain / loaded-state checks in the integration.
clusters.trigger: An integration service handler defining its own _async_get_config_entry-style function that looks up hass.config_entries by id and raises ServiceValidationError for missing/unloaded entries.

clusters.rule: When an entity platform method maps a Home Assistant enum value onto a vendor constant, validate membership before indexing and raise HomeAssistantError, so an unsupported mode never escapes as a raw KeyError.
clusters.trigger: An async_set_* entity method indexing a module-level HA-to-vendor mapping dict (e.g. HVAC_TO_WF_MODE[hvac_mode]) inside a try block that only catches library or ValueError exceptions.

clusters.rule: Do not add strings.json entries or icons for preset modes that already exist as core common presets; use the core PRESET_* constants in code and let the built-in translations and icons apply.
clusters.trigger: New state_attributes.preset_mode entries in an integration's strings.json or icons.json naming standard presets such as eco, comfort, away, boost.

clusters.rule: Do not create entities for static device metadata; firmware version, mDNS name and similar constants belong in the device registry entry, not in the state machine.
clusters.trigger: A new sensor entity description whose value is a device identity or configuration constant (firmware version, mdns name, serial, IP) rather than a changing measurement, even under EntityCategory.DIAGNOSTIC.

clusters.rule: Key an entity's icons.json entry by the exact translation_key set on its entity description, not by the sensor's internal key.
clusters.trigger: An added icons.json entity key under a platform that does not literally match the translation_key of the corresponding EntityDescription.

clusters.rule: Bound any integration-held cache keyed by a client- or peer-supplied identifier with a global cap or TTL, not just a per-key size limit.
clusters.trigger: A dict on an integration object indexed by an externally supplied id (session id, request id) that is written on inbound messages and only pruned per entry.

clusters.rule: Include the idle notification value 0 in not_states for Z-Wave notification binary sensors so the entity clears when the device reports idle.
clusters.trigger: A NotificationZWaveJSEntityDescription whose not_states set lists only the specific event enum members and omits 0.

clusters.rule: Adding a NewZWaveDiscoverySchema for a value that a legacy DISCOVERY_SCHEMAS entry already matches must preserve the existing entities: set allow_multi and adjust the legacy catch-all's not_states, or migrate the whole notification type and add it to MIGRATED_NOTIFICATION_TYPES.
clusters.trigger: A new NewZWaveDiscoverySchema entry in zwave_js covering a notification value or command class that legacy discovery schemas already produce entities for.

clusters.rule: Gate a report_usage deprecation warning on the deprecated condition actually being present, so callers that do not use the deprecated pattern never see it logged.
clusters.trigger: A report_usage call with breaks_in_ha_version placed on a common code path in core helpers without a check that the deprecated feature is in use.

clusters.rule: Keep a guard that prevents a registry's _async_load from running more than once.
clusters.trigger: Removal of the loaded-event assertions or any other once-only guard from a registry _async_load in homeassistant/helpers.

clusters.rule: Do not assume a sibling registry is set up when one registry helper calls another; guard dr.async_get / er.async_get so lookups still work with mocked or partially initialised registries.
clusters.trigger: A new dr.async_get(self._hass) or er.async_get(hass) call added inside an entity_registry or device_registry method that previously touched only its own data.

clusters.rule: Do not key a long-lived registry or cache by entity_id; entity_id changes at runtime on registry rename, so track the key used at insert time or keep it in sync on entity_id updates.
clusters.trigger: A module-level or hass-data dict indexed by entity.entity_id in async_added_to_hass and deleted by entity.entity_id in async_will_remove_from_hass.

clusters.rule: Match entity registry entries on domain and platform in addition to unique_id; unique_id alone is not unique across integrations.
clusters.trigger: An entity_registry_updated event handler or registry lookup whose condition tests only entry.unique_id against a set of known ids.

clusters.rule: Keep the dependency between core helper modules one-way: do not add a top-level import that closes a cycle between helpers modules; use a function-local import or move the logic into the module that already owns the dependency.
clusters.trigger: A new top-level `from .<helper> import ...` in homeassistant/helpers/ where the imported module already imports the importing one.

clusters.rule: Use plain string values, not enum members, in selector option and mode lists so voluptuous validation errors show the user-facing string rather than an enum repr.
clusters.trigger: A selector constant in homeassistant/helpers/selector.py listing StrEnum members that are later fed to vol.In or exposed in a selector config.

clusters.rule: When deprecating a Python dependency, update DEPRECATED_PACKAGES in homeassistant/requirements.py and the FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES entry in script/hassfest/requirements.py together, including the replacement package named in the reason text.
clusters.trigger: A change to the DEPRECATED_PACKAGES dict in homeassistant/requirements.py with no matching change to FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES in script/hassfest/requirements.py.

clusters.rule: Keep the pylint plugin README's description of a checker's accepted and rejected patterns exactly in step with the checker implementation and its test cases.
clusters.trigger: A change to pylint/plugins/README.md or a checker module docstring describing which code shapes the checker accepts, without a matching implementation or test in pylint/plugins/pylint_home_assistant/checkers/.

clusters.rule: Custom pylint checkers must key on the exact AST shape they target: handle the keyword form (service_func=) as well as the positional argument, and inspect the argument node type rather than merely counting arguments.
clusters.trigger: A checker helper extracting a handler from hass.services.async_register / async_register_admin_service by call.args index only, or a condition such as `if node.args and not has_translation_key` that never inspects the node type.

clusters.rule: Keep file-glob constants in script/ tooling identical to the paths: filter of the GitHub workflow that invokes them.
clusters.trigger: A TRACKED_PATTERNS-style glob tuple in script/ that is narrower than the paths: filter of the corresponding .github/workflows/*.yml.

clusters.rule: New hassfest validation must ship with hassfest tests exercising both the valid case and each distinct failure mode it can report.
clusters.trigger: A new validation branch in script/hassfest/*.py that adds an error message, with no corresponding case added under tests/hassfest/.

clusters.rule: When a config flow gains a fallback path, add a test for its success case end to end, not only for the error case that motivated it.
clusters.trigger: A new branch in an integration's config_flow.py that calls the client on a cache miss, with test_config_flow.py changes covering only the failure outcome.

clusters.rule: When a platform converts raw API values into device_class or state_class enums, add a test feeding a missing or invalid value and assert setup does not raise and the entity is still created with the attribute unset.
clusters.trigger: New SensorDeviceClass/SensorStateClass enum lookups on payload data in an integration's sensor.py, with tests covering only well-formed payloads.

clusters.rule: Do not assert exact library call counts during setup; assert the resulting device and entity registry state instead.
clusters.trigger: An assertion of the form `assert mock_client.<method>.call_count == N` in an integration test covering config entry setup.

clusters.rule: A test's name and docstring must describe exactly the platform, service and outcome its assertions cover; when a copied or parametrized test disagrees with its body, fix whichever of the two is wrong before merge.
clusters.trigger: A module or test docstring naming a different platform, service, or exception than the file/body asserts - including a docstring copied from a neighbouring test, or one describing only a subset of the parametrize list.

clusters.rule: Drive a test's expected end state with a realistic mock sequence (raise once, then return data) rather than an always-raising mock that reaches the expected state only through internal retry or swallowing.
clusters.trigger: A test parametrized over ConfigEntryState.LOADED whose client mock has an unconditional side_effect exception on the data-fetch method.

clusters.rule: Tests must use the integration's and core's own constants and helpers - DOMAIN, CONF_*, STATE_*, identifier helpers - wherever a value has a name, including as the key of the config dict passed to async_setup_component and in config entry data and options.
clusters.trigger: A raw string literal such as the domain name, "unavailable" or a config/option key in a test or conftest where the integration or homeassistant.const already defines a constant, or an identifier recomputed inline where the integration has a helper.

clusters.rule: Do not stack repeated await hass.async_block_till_done() calls to make a fixture settle; use a single deterministic wait or document why more than one pass is required.
clusters.trigger: Two or more consecutive `await hass.async_block_till_done()` statements in a test or conftest fixture.

clusters.rule: Mock an integration's library with AsyncMock-based fixtures rather than hand-written fake client classes.
clusters.trigger: A new conftest.py defining a stub class that reimplements the vendor library's properties and setters instead of patching the client with AsyncMock.

clusters.rule: When core code branches on whether the caller is a built-in integration (module starting with homeassistant.components.), test both the warning branch and the suppression branch.
clusters.trigger: A new report/warning in homeassistant/ that is skipped for modules under homeassistant.components., with tests asserting only the warning case.

clusters.rule: Match the mock to the real callable: patch coroutine functions with new_callable=AsyncMock (a plain patch(..., return_value=...) yields a non-awaitable MagicMock), patch synchronous ones with MagicMock, and never spec a whole library object as AsyncMock when it also exposes synchronous listener or registration methods.
clusters.trigger: patch("<library>.<Class>.<async_method>", return_value=...) without new_callable=AsyncMock, or a patch / AsyncMock(spec=...) / fixture annotation whose sync-vs-async kind does not match the awaited-ness of the target in the integration code.

clusters.rule: Do not write generated entity_ids into tests by hand: resolve the entity through the entity registry by unique_id or config entry and assert on the resolved id, including when asserting that an entity was not created.
clusters.trigger: A literal entity_id string built from a device name slug, or an assertion that `hass.states.get("<domain>.<guessed_slug>") is None`, especially for names whose characters change the slug ("2+", "2-way").

clusters.rule: Assert that `hass.states.get(entity_id)` returned a state object before dereferencing `.state`.
clusters.trigger: A test chains `hass.states.get(...).state` in an assertion or comprehension without a preceding `is not None` check.

clusters.rule: Every parameter of a test function, including injected fixtures, must carry a type annotation.
clusters.trigger: A new `async def test_*` adds a fixture parameter (e.g. `mock_growatt_v1_api`) with no annotation while its siblings are annotated.

clusters.rule: When new entities are added, regenerate and commit the snapshot files, and keep any hard-coded expected entity list in the same order the entity descriptions are iterated during setup.
clusters.trigger: A PR adds entity descriptions to a platform's description tuple and adds matching entries to a test's expected-entity list or snapshot assertion.

clusters.rule: Do not land test scaffolding nothing consumes: conftest fixtures, JSON fixture files, module-level TEST_* constants and fixture parameters in a test signature must each be referenced by a test in the same PR, or removed.
clusters.trigger: A diff adding a fixture, a file under tests/components/*/fixtures/, a helper such as init_*_integration, or a test-signature parameter (snapshot, a client/coordinator fixture) that no test in the diff references - or leaving one behind after the test that used it changed.

clusters.rule: Shared mock/data construction repeated across tests belongs in a pytest fixture in conftest.py, not in module-level builder functions each test calls manually.
clusters.trigger: A test module defines a helper like `build_homeegrams()` or inline mock-client wiring and calls it in an identical setup block before `setup_integration` in several tests.

clusters.rule: Timestamps passed to `freezer.move_to()` must carry an explicit timezone offset when the assertions depend on local-time conversion.
clusters.trigger: A test calls `freezer.move_to("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS")` with no `Z`/`+00:00` suffix while the code under test branches on `dt_util.now().hour`.

clusters.rule: Stateless entity triggers must accept STATE_UNKNOWN as a valid from_state so the first real event after startup fires, matching button entity trigger semantics.
clusters.trigger: A trigger implementation or its parametrized tests treat an `unknown` -> first-matching-state transition as not triggering for a stateless domain (event, button).

clusters.rule: Service actions that resolve a device_id must have test coverage for the device being absent from the device registry, and should raise ServiceValidationError rather than failing silently.
clusters.trigger: A new service handler takes `device_id` and looks it up in the device registry, with tests only covering the happy path and backend errors.

clusters.rule: Assert that a specific mocked method was or was not awaited instead of inspecting `mock.mock_calls[-1]`.
clusters.trigger: A test indexes into `mock_calls` (e.g. `mock_calls[-1][0] != "send_start_impulse_async"`) to prove a call did not happen.

clusters.rule: Parametrized tests for capability/feature flag enums must cover the combined-flags and zero/empty value, not only the single-flag cases.
clusters.trigger: A platform change alters how bitwise capability flags are interpreted while the test parametrization lists only individual enum members.

clusters.rule: After firing a coordinator's update timer with `async_fire_time_changed`, await `hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)` before asserting on refreshed state.
clusters.trigger: A test ticks the freezer by the coordinator UPDATE_INTERVAL, calls `async_fire_time_changed`, then asserts entity state after a plain `await hass.async_block_till_done()`.

clusters.rule: Run the translation generation script for the integration and re-capture entity snapshots after adding translation keys, so snapshotted entities show their translated names and object-id-derived entity_ids.
clusters.trigger: A snapshot .ambr adds entities with a `translation_key` set but `original_name: None`, no `object_id_base`, and generic entity_ids like `sensor.device_1_2`.

clusters.rule: Do not snapshot volatile numeric sensor readings; snapshot the stable entity metadata (entity id, device class, unit, availability) and relax the fluctuating `state` value.
clusters.trigger: A dependency bump changes numeric `state` values inside a snapshot .ambr file, forcing snapshot churn.

clusters.rule: Snapshot the device registry entry once per test module, not once per entity.
clusters.trigger: A per-platform test loops over entity registry entries and snapshots the resolved `device_entry` inside the loop.

clusters.rule: A regenerated snapshot must contain exactly one entity per unique_id for a config entry; prune stale blocks instead of committing duplicates.
clusters.trigger: A snapshot .ambr contains two entries sharing a unique_id under different entity_ids.

clusters.rule: A test must actually exercise the failure path named in its name and docstring; patch the dependency with a failing `side_effect` rather than a benign empty result that duplicates an existing test.
clusters.trigger: A config flow test named for a startup/discovery failure patches the discovery helper to return an empty result and asserts a generic abort reason.

clusters.rule: Tests that enable a disabled-by-default entity must advance time to run the coordinator refresh and assert the entity's resolved value, not merely that the entity exists.
clusters.trigger: A test enables an entity via the entity registry and reloads, then only asserts `state is not None`.

clusters.rule: Obtain registries through the provided pytest fixtures (`entity_registry: er.EntityRegistry`, `device_registry`, `issue_registry`) declared as test/fixture parameters, not by calling `er.async_get(hass)` inside the body.
clusters.trigger: A test or conftest fixture body calls `er.async_get(hass)` / `dr.async_get(hass)` instead of taking the registry fixture.

clusters.rule: Assert that a specific repair issue key is absent rather than that the whole issue registry is empty.
clusters.trigger: A test asserts `len(issue_registry.issues) == 0` or compares the full issue registry contents.

clusters.rule: Deprecation repair issues must have test coverage for every branch that selects a different translation key, including the entity-used-in-automations/scripts variant and its placeholder substitution.
clusters.trigger: A repairs test only covers the plain deprecated-entity issue while the implementation also raises a `*_scripts`/`*_automations` variant with an `{items}` placeholder.

clusters.rule: When a change tightens validation, fix the existing tests it breaks instead of deleting them.
clusters.trigger: A diff that adds stricter validation also removes an existing test function.

clusters.rule: When a service response model gains fields, add a test case where those fields carry non-default values rather than only the default None case.
clusters.trigger: A test's expected service-response dict gains new keys whose asserted values are all `None`.

clusters.rule: A test parametrized over a fixture name must take that fixture as a function parameter; otherwise drop the parametrization.
clusters.trigger: @pytest.mark.parametrize("<fixture_name>", [...]) - mqtt_config_entry_data, clients_all_payload - above a test whose signature omits that name.

clusters.rule: Unique_id migration tests must round-trip every unique_id format the integration produces (device, multi-channel and group variants) and must not let one format's pattern match another's ids.
clusters.trigger: A migration test derives old-format unique_ids with string slicing/suffix matching and skips entries where the channel is None.

clusters.rule: Tests for a trigger or condition must cover the full domain matrix its implementation accepts: every supported entity domain, plus a negative case proving unsupported domains do not match.
clusters.trigger: A new trigger/condition test parametrized over a single domain (e.g. only "person") while the implementation also handles device_tracker or others, or covering only supported domains with no unsupported-entity case, including under behavior='all'.

clusters.rule: Matter node fixtures must list any cluster whose attributes they define in that endpoint's Descriptor ServerList.
clusters.trigger: A `tests/components/matter/fixtures/nodes/*.json` adds attributes for a cluster id that is absent from the endpoint's `65531` server list.

clusters.rule: Setup-failure tests must assert the exception whose retry semantics match the intent: ConfigEntryNotReady when setup should be retried, ConfigEntryError when the failure is fatal.
clusters.trigger: A test named or documented as "not ready" asserts ConfigEntryError (or vice versa) around async_setup_entry.

clusters.rule: Service-call tests must pass values that are valid under the service schema (the integration's direction/mode constants), not stand-in primitives.
clusters.trigger: A test invokes an integration service or helper with integers/placeholders where the service schema expects domain constants such as DIR_LEFT/DIR_UP.

clusters.rule: Bluetooth integration tests must drive the integration through the public injection helpers (e.g. inject_bluetooth_service_info) rather than calling a coordinator's private _async_handle_bluetooth_event.
clusters.trigger: A test calls coordinator._async_handle_bluetooth_event(...) or another underscore-prefixed coordinator callback to simulate an advertisement.

clusters.rule: Do not re-serialize existing JSON test fixtures; leave non-ASCII text as literal UTF-8 rather than \u escapes.
clusters.trigger: A diff in tests/components/*/fixtures/*.json rewrites accented characters as \uXXXX escapes or otherwise reformats untouched fixture lines.

clusters.rule: Tests must not assert known-incorrect integration behavior as the expected value; leave the assertion out or mark it xfail until the integration is fixed.
clusters.trigger: A parametrized test case is accompanied by a comment calling the expected value a known bug or a follow-up fix.

clusters.rule: Patch third-party helpers at the integration's import site (homeassistant.components.<domain>.<name>) rather than patching the library or stdlib module globally.
clusters.trigger: A test calls patch("shutil.which", ...) or patch("<library>.<func>", ...) for a symbol the integration imported into its own module namespace.

clusters.rule: Give each entity a translation_key so its name (and therefore its entity_id suffix) is distinct from the device name instead of the entity_id collapsing to button.<device>.
clusters.trigger: A new entity snapshot shows original_name/object_id_base as None and an entity_id equal to the bare device or container slug.

clusters.rule: Media source tests must construct MediaSourceItem with the integration's own DOMAIN and a bare item identifier, not another integration's domain or a full media-source:// URI.
clusters.trigger: MediaSourceItem(hass, "<other-domain>", f"{media_source.URI_SCHEME}{DOMAIN}", ...) in a media source test.

clusters.rule: Recorder platform unit-conversion maps must be string-to-string; do not use None keys or empty-string units in the mapping.
clusters.trigger: A recorder platform test or implementation supplies a unit map entry like {None: ""} where the annotation is dict[str, dict[str, str]].

clusters.rule: Syrupy .ambr files must be produced by running pytest --snapshot-update; never hand-write, hand-append or hand-edit snapshot blocks or their parametrization ids.
clusters.trigger: A diff to tests/components/*/snapshots/*.ambr that deviates from generator output - a manually written EntityRegistryEntrySnapshot block, a duplicated '# ---' divider, or a bracketed id ([megane_e-tech]) that does not match the parametrize source values.

clusters.rule: Tests must not mutate a shared module-level CONFIG dict; copy it and set options on the nested integration config the integration actually reads.
clusters.trigger: A test assigns into a module-level CONFIG constant (config[CONF_X] = ...) rather than building a local copy of the nested domain config.

clusters.rule: Import SnapshotAssertion from syrupy.assertion and snapshot_platform from tests.common; do not pull SnapshotAssertion out of tests.common.
clusters.trigger: A test file adds `from tests.common import SnapshotAssertion` (alone or alongside snapshot_platform).

clusters.rule: Config entry migration tests must seed the entity registry with the entities a pre-migration install would already have, and assert they are re-associated with the new device or subentry.
clusters.trigger: A migration test asserts only that subentries/devices were created, without registering the old entities beforehand.

clusters.rule: Tests must not branch on entity_id with if/elif to pick expected values; parametrize the expected state alongside the entity or use the snapshot_platform helper.
clusters.trigger: An if/elif chain inside a test loop selecting which assertion to run per entity_id.

clusters.rule: Helpers that mutate a BluetoothServiceInfoBleak must copy the existing manufacturer_data mapping and update only the target manufacturer id, not replace the whole dict.
clusters.trigger: A bluetooth test helper builds `{<mfr_id>: bytes(...)}` and assigns it as the full manufacturer_data.

clusters.rule: Each device entry added to a shared API fixture must use a unique deviceId rather than reusing an existing device's identifier.
clusters.trigger: A new object appended to tests/components/*/fixtures/*.json repeats a deviceId already present in the file.

clusters.rule: A mock or fixture must configure every library call and accessor the exercised path touches - including calls whose exceptions the integration suppresses, and the availability accessor the base entity reads - matching the fixture combination the integration's existing tests already use.
clusters.trigger: A test mocking one of a pair of related API calls (mock_setup_webhook without get_webhook_configuration), or a Mock(spec=<device class>) fixture omitting a *.return_value that the sibling fixtures in the same conftest set (e.g. get_online.return_value).

clusters.rule: Replacement functions substituted for a library API in tests must accept *args and **kwargs so they match the real call surface.
clusters.trigger: A test defines a zero-argument stub (e.g. an async generator) that replaces a library method the integration calls with arguments.

clusters.rule: Name a platform test after the Home Assistant service it calls rather than the underlying vendor concept.
clusters.trigger: A test that calls a service such as vacuum.clean_area is renamed to describe the implementation detail (test_clean_segments).

clusters.rule: Advance coordinator intervals with freezer.tick(...) followed by async_fire_time_changed(hass); do not pass a separately computed dt_util.utcnow() + timedelta timestamp.
clusters.trigger: async_fire_time_changed(hass, dt_util.utcnow() + timedelta(...)) in a test that also uses the freezer fixture.

clusters.rule: An empty-string unit from a device payload must be normalized to None (or mapped to a real unit) rather than surfacing as unit_of_measurement: ''.
clusters.trigger: A discovery path or fixture carries "unit": "" for a numeric datapoint and passes it through to the entity description.

clusters.rule: Tests that assert on debug log output must raise the level first with caplog.set_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="homeassistant.components.<domain>").
clusters.trigger: A test asserts a debug-level message appears in caplog.text without calling caplog.set_level for the integration's logger.

clusters.rule: Read entity metadata that is not exposed in the state through the entity registry, not by reaching into hass.data["entity_components"].
clusters.trigger: A test does hass.data["entity_components"]["<platform>"].get_entity(entity_id) to inspect an entity object.

clusters.rule: When an entity key change alters generated entity_ids, update every remaining reference to the old entity_id in the test module.
clusters.trigger: A parametrization renames sensor keys (device_cpu -> cpu) while other tests in the file still assert on the old entity_id string.

clusters.rule: Never wait on wall-clock time with asyncio.sleep in tests; patch the delay or call_later so timers fire deterministically.
clusters.trigger: await asyncio.sleep(<n>) used to let a scheduled callback or timer fire in a test.

clusters.rule: Assert against concrete expected values (such as the generated proxy URL prefix) rather than comparing two attributes of the object under test, which holds by construction.
clusters.trigger: assert obj.attr_a == obj.attr_b where both come from the same entity under test and the implementation makes them equal.

clusters.rule: A snapshot_platform test for a platform that contains entities with entity_registry_enabled_default=False must apply @pytest.mark.usefixtures("entity_registry_enabled_by_default"), because snapshot_platform asserts disabled_by is None for every entity.
clusters.trigger: A new or edited test calls snapshot_platform(hass, entity_registry, snapshot, entry.entry_id) for a platform whose entity descriptions include entity_registry_enabled_default=False, without the entity_registry_enabled_by_default fixture.

clusters.rule: An entity registry snapshot whose 'aliases' field renders as list([None]) must be investigated as an entity-registration bug; aliases must be an empty set or a set of non-null strings.
clusters.trigger: A new .ambr snapshot contains "'aliases': list([\n None,\n ])" inside an EntityRegistryEntrySnapshot.

clusters.rule: A test that patches an API call to raise an authentication exception must assert that the reauth flow actually started (e.g. config_entry_reauth.assert_called_once()), not merely reference the mock.
clusters.trigger: A test injects an authentication exception via side_effect and references a reauth mock without calling an assertion method on it.

clusters.rule: Reconfigure-flow tests that submit only a subset of the config entry fields must assert that the omitted optional fields (credentials, tokens) are preserved on the entry.
clusters.trigger: A test_config_flow.py reconfigure test calls async_configure with a dict omitting CONF_USERNAME/CONF_PASSWORD or other optional entry keys and only asserts the flow result type.

clusters.rule: When firing async_fire_time_changed to trigger a coordinator refresh, capture the base time after the config entries are set up (or add a margin / use fire_all=True); a time captured before setup can land before the timer the entity scheduled.
clusters.trigger: A test assigns now = dt_util.now()/utcnow() before async_setup_component or hass.config_entries.async_setup, then calls async_fire_time_changed(hass, now + <scan interval>) and asserts on refresh call counts.

clusters.rule: Config entry migration tests must be named (and their docstring worded) for the exact version transition exercised, e.g. test_migrate_minor_version_1_to_2 rather than test_migrate_to_1_1.
clusters.trigger: A test in tests/components/*/test_init.py exercises async_migrate_entry / minor_version or version bumps but its name does not state the source and target version.

clusters.rule: Fixtures that build a MockConfigEntry must derive its title, data and options from the parametrizable config fixture rather than hard-coding literals.
clusters.trigger: A conftest.py fixture constructs MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, title="<literal>", ...) while a sibling get_config/mock_config fixture supplies the same value and can be overridden by tests.

clusters.rule: Tests must address entities by their hard-coded entity ID (as captured in the snapshot) instead of looking the ID up dynamically from the entity registry.
clusters.trigger: A test calls er.async_entries_for_config_entry(...) and filters by domain/platform just to recover a single entity_id for a service call or state assertion.

clusters.rule: Test docstrings must state only the behavior under test; do not narrate device model history, the prior bug, or the PR description in them.
clusters.trigger: A new test's docstring spans multiple paragraphs describing a specific device firmware quirk, the exception it used to raise, or the regression history.

clusters.rule: Changes to shared trigger/helper base classes must add coverage for subclasses that intentionally target STATE_UNKNOWN/STATE_UNAVAILABLE before excluding those states globally.
clusters.trigger: A diff makes an EntityTriggerBase-style helper skip unavailable/unknown states in match logic, and the accompanying tests only use an implementation whose is_valid_state() rejects those states.

clusters.rule: A fix for an async race must ship a regression test that actually drives both concurrent call paths; asserting a new private flag (e.g. script_obj._unloaded) does not substitute for reproducing the race.
clusters.trigger: A PR adds unload/teardown guard state to a helper and its test only asserts the private attribute instead of starting a run while the unload is in progress.

clusters.rule: Test cases added to the custom pylint quality-scale checkers must encode a rule the checker deliberately enforces; incidental matches produced by the implementation should be dropped or the implementation adjusted.
clusters.trigger: A new parametrized case in tests/pylint/quality_scale/ asserts a diagnostic on code whose flagged condition cannot occur in practice (e.g. _attr_unique_id assignment after a raise in __init__).

clusters.rule: Changes to the split_tests fixture-hashing logic must add coverage proving the hash changes when a shared helper module above or beside the chosen root is edited, not only for conftest.py files.
clusters.trigger: A diff modifies fixture-hash computation in script/split_tests and its tests only cover conftest.py edits and same-directory scope.

clusters.rule: End-to-end frontend tests must assert on the element of the specific step under test, not on the outer shell component that renders before its API call resolves.
clusters.trigger: A Playwright spec asserts only expect(page.locator("ha-onboarding")).toBeVisible() (or another shell element) after navigating, without waiting for the concrete step element.
